stepthru › Grids › Shortest path in a maze

Shortest path in a maze, step by step

Breadth-first search on a grid finds the shortest path through a maze. It reaches cells in order of distance, so the first time it reaches the exit is along a shortest path.

Click the figure, then use ← →, space, Home and End, or the buttons.

How it works

  1. Write 0 in the start cell and put it in a queue.
  2. Take the cell at the front of the queue.
  3. For each open neighbor not reached yet: write its distance, remember where it was reached from, and add it to the queue.
  4. Stop when the exit is reached.
  5. Walk back from the exit along the cells each one was reached from.

Cost

Time
O(rows · cols): each cell is reached once.
Space
O(rows · cols) for the queue and the distances.
Needs
Every move to cost the same. With weights, use Dijkstra's algorithm.

The code behind this figure

Nothing here is hand-animated. The figure comes from this code: a plain shortest path in a maze with stepthru tracer calls, such as set and mark, that record each step.
